figma.typographyRule: Inter for all UI labels/copy/nav/headers/breadcrumb/status text/worker names (per DESIGN.md 5.2); JetBrains Mono for technical values only — job IDs, metric values (concurrency count, queue count, last-job timestamp, success-rate percentage, job duration) — matching DESIGN.md section 20's example layout and section 5.2's rule to use monospace for Job IDs/Worker IDs/API-technical values.
figma.responsiveRules: Desktop (1440px frames): 240px fixed sidebar, single content column (1136px) with page title + subtitle, a 3-column row of Worker Status Cards (Scanner/Flagger/Scheduler — concurrency, queue, last job, success rate, colored status dot+label), and a Recent Jobs table below (Job ID/Worker/Status/Duration/Finished columns, status shown with colored dot+text never color alone). Degraded state adds a full-width warning Alert banner above the cards and highlights the affected worker's card with an amber border. Mobile (375px reference frame, content-fit height): hand-built hamburger Mobile Header replaces Header+Sidebar; single-column stacked worker cards with condensed queue/success-rate summary line (Recent Jobs table omitted on mobile as a deliberate content-priority reduction, consistent with DESIGN.md 9.2's 'tables become horizontally scrollable or transform into stacked rows' — here reduced to essential per-worker status only, matching the mobile precedent set by M02/M04's own table-heavy screens).
scopeNotes: An 'Empty' state was not designed: worker monitoring by definition always has exactly 3 workers (Scanner, Flagger, Scheduler) per ARCHITECTURE.md's fixed worker-process architecture — there is no realistic zero-workers scenario to design for, consistent with FIGMA_WORKFLOW.md's 'do not create fake states that are not supported by the product' rule.

'Degraded' was designed as the meaningful non-happy-path state instead of a generic 'disabled' state, since DESIGN.md section 20 and ARCHITECTURE.md describe worker health as Healthy/Degraded/Down-style operational states, not an enable/disable toggle (workers are always-running background processes, not user-configurable like Scan Rules).

Recent Jobs table on mobile was intentionally omitted rather than force-fit into a horizontally-scrolling table, in favor of the condensed per-worker summary line already present on each stacked card — a deliberate content-priority decision for the operational-monitoring use case, not an oversight.
Placed on existing page '05 — Admin' (node 3:6), in a new column (x=14520 onward) clear of M06's Review Queue block and M08/M09's columns, with 120px+ gaps maintained throughout.
Did not design Scan Rules, Templates, Users, Marketing, Auth, Tokens, Overview, Findings-list, Finding-detail, or Review Queue screens — all out of scope for M10 and belong to other modules.

knownIssues: No generic Worker Status/Queue Status Figma component exists as an instanceable primitive (pre-existing gap, see figma.knownIssues below) — worker cards hand-composed in code too, matching the Figma pass.

Worker health status (healthy/degraded) is derived heuristically from a 10-job recent-completion sample per queue, not a true process-level heartbeat/liveness signal — acceptable given ARCHITECTURE.md has no WorkerJob/heartbeat table; a future module could add one for a stronger liveness guarantee.

Recent Jobs list is a merged best-effort sample (10 most recent completed/failed per queue, capped at 10 overall) rather than a fully paginated job history — sufficient for the Figma-designed operational-glance UI, not a full audit log.

backend.summary: lib/workers.ts reads worker health/queue metrics directly from BullMQ (getJobCounts + getJobs) across the 3 fixed queues (scan-queue, flag-queue, scheduler-queue) — no new Prisma table/migration needed since BullMQ/Redis is already the durable source of truth for job state. GET /api/workers (admin-only, requireAdmin) returns { workers, recentJobs, degraded }. Status derived healthy/degraded from recent completed/failed sample ratio (threshold 50%, min 3 samples). Concurrency values (2/3/1) mirror the literal values apps/worker constructs its BullMQ Workers with.

frontend.summary: Admin / Workers page at /admin/workers implements all 5 Figma states: Default (3 worker cards + Recent Jobs table), Loading (route-level loading.tsx skeletons), Error (ErrorState + Retry), Degraded (amber Alert banner + amber-bordered affected card), Mobile (condensed per-worker summary line, table omitted per Figma scopeNotes). Polls GET /api/workers every 15s for near-live health. Sidebar already linked here from an earlier module pass; route now exists and resolves.

integration.summary: Server Component (page.tsx) fetches initial snapshot via lib/workers.ts directly; WorkersClient polls the real /api/workers endpoint for refresh and manual Retry. Full path verified: Figma design -> frontend -> API route -> lib/workers.ts -> BullMQ/Redis (same queues apps/worker writes to). No mock/fake data in the shipped module.

testStatus.summary: typecheck (tsc --noEmit): clean. lint (next lint via eslint on changed files): clean. next build: succeeds, /admin/workers and /api/workers both compile as dynamic routes. vitest: 167/167 tests pass repo-wide (10 new: 6 lib/workers.test.ts + 4 app/api/workers/route.test.ts), 0 regressions.

securityStatus.summary: Module handles zero token/secret data (worker/queue/job metadata only) — grepped clean. GET /api/workers gated by requireAdmin() (401 unauthenticated / 403 non-admin) plus existing middleware.ts ADMIN-only gate on /admin/:path*. Error responses return a generic message only, no internals/stack leaked. No new input surface requiring validation (GET only, no body/params).
